- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to first 5 forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.5), model exhibits overfitting to recent history; smooth forecast curve with 3–5 day moving average filter.
- If last 3 sentiment values are negative and cumulative sum < -1.0, model tends to forecast lower than true; add 0.8–1.2% upward adjustment.
- Model often misses mean reversion in 10–15 day horizon; if price deviates >3σ from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean with 2–3 day lag.
